candidates.attacker_control: The attacker-controlled input is the content (entry names) of the Node/npm archive that the tooling downloads and extracts. The archive is fetched through DefaultFileDownloader (https or file: scheme, lines 82-86) from a configurable nodeDownloadRoot (NodeTasks.Builder default https://nodejs.org/dist/, NodeTasks.java:120-121; configurable via the 'node.download.root' Maven property, FlowModeAbstractMojo.java:108). No checksum or signature of the archive is verified before extraction, so a malicious/compromised mirror, an on-path attacker against a non-TLS mirror, or a crafted archive referenced via a file: root can deliver '../'-laden zip entries. It is not directly controllable via an HTTP request to a running server.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: The tar branch in the same class does enforce containment (lines 134-148), showing the missing zip check is not a repository-wide design decision. Default nodeDownloadRoot is HTTPS nodejs.org (TLS 1.2 is forced in DefaultFileDownloader.download), so the default configuration requires an on-path/compromised-mirror position; the file: scheme branch and custom mirror property widen this. The archive is not attacker-supplied over HTTP, so this is not a remote-triggerable-by-request issue. No test sources are present in the snapshot to confirm intended behavior.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write outside the intended extraction directory, with the privileges of the build/dev-mode process. Files written this way are subsequently read/executed by the toolchain (the freshly installed node executable, npm/webpack scripts, project or user configuration), so this can lead to execution of attacker-supplied content or persistent integrity compromise of the development/build host. At minimum it is an out-of-directory file overwrite (denial of service / data destruction).
candidates.prerequisites: The Node-install path must run and the archive must be a .zip: Platform.OS.getArchiveExtension() returns 'zip' on Windows (Platform.java:88-93) and 'tar.gz' elsewhere, so Windows hosts (or custom zip archives served from a mirror) exercise the unchecked branch. The extraction runs with the file permissions of the Maven/build or dev-mode JVM user.
candidates.root_cause: extractZipArchive builds 'new File(destinationDirectory + File.separator + entry.getName())' (lines 88-90), calls prepDestination(destPath, entry.isDirectory()) (line 91) and writes contents with copyZipFileContents(...) (line 93, FileOutputStream at lines 117-121) without ever verifying that the canonical destination path remains inside destinationDirectory. ZipEntry names may contain '../' (or Windows-style separators), so extraction can escape the install/temp directory. The tar.gz branch of the same class does perform this validation (extractGzipTarArchive: canonicalDestinationDirectory at lines 134-135 plus startsWithPath check at lines 143-148), which makes the omission in the zip branch an inconsistency, not an intentional design documented anywhere in the file.
candidates.title: Zip Slip: zip entries extracted without containment check in DefaultArchiveExtractor.extractZipArchive
candidates.trace: FrontendTools.installNode (FrontendTools.java:440-456) -> NodeInstaller.install (NodeInstaller.java:197-220) -> installNode(data) -> extractFile(data.getArchive(), data.getTmpDirectory()) (NodeInstaller.java:245-257, 404-409) -> DefaultArchiveExtractor.extract (DefaultArchiveExtractor.java:45-60) dispatches on '.zip' (line 51-52) to extractZipArchive (81-98) -> prepDestination/createNewFile + copyZipFileContents writes to File(destinationDirectory + File.separator + entry.getName()) with no canonical containment check.
candidates.unverified: Not executed or dynamically confirmed; the exact upstream fix/CVE mapping is unknown; attacker's ability to influence the downloaded archive depends on configuration or network position, so exploitability is not proven from source alone. The '..' path is normalized by java.io.File only in the sense that it follows the parent reference, which is why it escapes, but no runtime check was performed.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Path Traversal (Zip Slip) leading to arbitrary file write

coverage_summary: Scope per get_source_scope: 1891 model-visible files, no over-size/symlink/sensitive-path exclusions; binary-like files are skipped by the reader. The snapshot contains only main sources (no test sources are present). I reviewed flow-server HTTP entry points and handlers (BootstrapHandler, WebComponentBootstrapHandler/WebComponentProvider, VaadinServlet/VaadinServletService/StaticFileServer/WebJarServer/PwaHandler/DevModeHandler, UIDL/RPC handlers, push, stream receiver/resource handling, router internals, frontend installer), plus partial reviews of flow-client (client engine, ExecuteJavaScriptProcessor, RouterLinkHandler, SystemErrorHandler, dev-mode gizmo), flow-html-components, flow-data, flow-maven-plugin and flow-migration build tooling. The selected candidate is in the frontend/node installer; the rest of the HTTP-facing surface reviewed here appeared to contain deployed mitigations (isPathUnsafe, CSRF key checks, constant-time comparisons, regex/whitelist restrictions).
limitations: No code execution, tests, or scanners were run; findings are static source evidence only.
No upstream/Git history or patch diff was available, so I could not confirm which security fix (if any) this snapshot predates; the CVE/ground-truth mapping is unknown.
Test sources are absent from the snapshot, so intended behavior and existing coverage could not be validated.

The selected candidate's attacker-control prerequisite (influence over the node archive) depends on configuration (node.download.root/file: root) or network position; default HTTPS download from nodejs.org reduces practical exploitability.
Review of flow-client, flow-data, and build-tool modules was sampling-based rather than exhaustive.

rejected_leads.lead: WebComponentBootstrapHandler.getServiceUrl uses the unvalidated request parameter 'url' as the base URL for generated script/link src attributes and as the service/push URL (flow-server/src/main/java/com/vaadin/flow/server/communication/WebComponentBootstrapHandler.java:432-447, used at 154-178, 214-217, 349-365).
rejected_leads.reason: Real security-relevant trust issue (possible open redirect / script-origin injection in web-component NPM mode), but the normal embedding flow auto-generates 'url' from the same-origin script src (WebComponentProvider.bootstrapNpm), and checkURL only rejects double quotes. Exploitation appears to require an embedder that forwards untrusted input into the url parameter; could not establish attacker control in the default flow, so it was not selected as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: WebJarServer.getWebJarPath performs a simple prefix replace to '/webjars/' and tryServeWebJarResource resolves it through ServletContext.getResource without HandlerHelper.isPathUnsafe (WebJarServer.java:100-150).
rejected_leads.reason: Traversal-looking path handling, but traversal paths are intercepted first by StaticFileServer.isStaticResourceRequest/serveStaticResource, which calls isPathUnsafe, and container normalization prevents '..' from surviving in getPathInfo in the default configuration.

rejected_leads.lead: HandlerHelper.isPathUnsafe decodes the path only once (HandlerHelper.java:198-208) and PARENT_DIRECTORY_REGEX requires a leading slash or backslash.
rejected_leads.reason: No demonstrated sink where a doubly/triply encoded path survives all decoders and reaches a file/resource lookup; classloader and ServletContext lookups do not re-decode percent escapes.

rejected_leads.lead: AtmospherePushConnection.FragmentedMessage.append trusts the client-declared message length and only enforces it with an assert (AtmospherePushConnection.java:76-111).
rejected_leads.reason: Could allow memory/CPU exhaustion in production (assertions disabled), but impact is DoS limited by what the client can send over push, and it was weaker than the selected file-write candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: BootstrapHandler.checkWebpackStatus inserts dev-mode webpack output as raw HTML (BootstrapHandler.java:583-600) and RouteNotFoundError builds HTML from the request path (RouteNotFoundError.java:46-68).
rejected_leads.reason: checkWebpackStatus is dev-mode only with locally generated process output; RouteNotFoundError already sanitizes path and additional info with Jsoup.clean(Whitelist.none()), so no injection was established.

summary: This is the Vaadin Flow 2.6-SNAPSHOT (Vaadin 14.6 line) repository. I reviewed the HTTP-facing server code (BootstrapHandler, WebComponent bootstrap/provider, UIDL/RPC handlers, push, stream resource/upload handling, static/webjar/PWA/dev-mode file serving, router), the client engine, and the frontend/node install tooling. The strongest concrete defect is in the Node archive extraction used by the Flow frontend tooling: the ZIP extraction branch concatenates attacker-controllable archive entry names to the destination path and writes them without verifying the resulting canonical path stays inside the destination, while the sibling tar.gz branch performs exactly that check. This is a classic Zip Slip (CWE-22) arbitrary-file-write pattern; on Windows the Node distribution is a .zip and is extracted through this path. Attack surface is indirect (archive content, not a direct HTTP parameter), so it is submitted as a lead with that caveat, not as a confirmed exploit.
